links.outcome: Calibration of LLM self-reported confidence against accuracy in phenotype predictions
links.effect: Self-confidence was only moderately informative. High-confidence predictions were more accurate, but larger models showed systematic overconfidence.
links.quote: Self-confidence calibration was only moderately informative: high-confidence predictions were more accurate, but larger models exhibited systematic overconfidence.

links.outcome: Prediction consistency (Shannon entropy) across prompting strategies and temperature
links.effect: Prediction entropy was low overall and driven mainly by phenotype difficulty rather than prompting or temperature.
links.quote: Prediction entropy was low overall and driven primarily by phenotype difficulty rather than prompting or temperature.

unlisted_practices: Whole-document inference versus text chunking for LLM phenotyping
Aggregation strategies (any-positive, two-vote, majority) across chunk-level predictions
Comparison of prompting strategies (zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought, extract-then-phenotype)
Choosing smaller open-weight models for cost efficiency versus larger commercial models

screen.reason: The study conducts a systematic factorial evaluation of deployment/pipeline design choices (prompting, text chunking, and voting/aggregation strategies) to determine best practices for LLM-based EHR phenotyping.

primary.practice: pipeline design optimization (prompting, chunking, and aggregation strategies)
